newsitem.title: USA: Republicans renominate Gingrich as House speaker.
newsitem.headline: Republicans renominate Gingrich as House speaker.

text.p: Republicans rallied around Newt Gingrich on Wednesday, nominating him for a second term as speaker of the House of Representatives despite concern about ethics charges swirling around the controversial Georgia conservative.
Gingrich was approved unanimously at a gathering of Republicans elected to the House in the November 5 vote that kept Republican majorities in both houses of Congress.
"This is a bittersweet day for me," Gingrich said in accepting the nomination. His stepfather, Robert Gingrich, died of cancer earlier in the day.
Republicans also re-elected Dick Armey as House majority leader and Tom Delay as his deputy. Both are from Texas.

Gingrich seems certain to be elected speaker by the full House membership when the new Congress convenes on Jan. 7. The vote is normally along straight party lines, and Republicans will have a majority of at least 20 seats in the 435-member House once a few undecided contests are resolved.
The only threat to Gingrich's re-election could arise if the House Ethics Committee makes damaging charges against him in a report expected to be issued before the end of the year.

The committee is investigating whether a tax-exempt foundation he formerly headed was used illegally for political purposes, and whether Gingrich had provided accurate information to the committee about a college course he taught.

Refering to Democratic attacks against him during the election, Gingrich said, "I'm still here, but it was painful." Democrats made him the focus of their campaign, blaming him for two unpopular government shutdowns last winter, and tried to link every Republican House candidate to him.
But Gingrich continued recent bipartisan efforts to talk up political harmony in Washington, promising to try to work with President Bill Clinton and congressional Democrats.
"We have an absolute moral obligation to make this system work," he said. "Working with President Clinton and Democrats who agree with us, we will continue to work for a balanced budget."
"We won't always agree on details but I want to suggest to you that if the last Congress was the confrontation Congress, this Congress will be the implementation Congress," he said.

He said his other goals included making the U.S. education system the best in the world and making Washington, D.C., a rundown city rife with crime with chaotic social and educational services, into the world's finest capital.
Washington's government and its financing are essentially controlled by Congress.
Gingrich said the United States must continue to lead the world and reject isolationism. He also called for a return to strong national moral values and a belief in God.
"What Newt is trying to do is return power to the people," Representative John Kasich of Ohio said in nominating Gingrich.
"Rarely have I met a person who has been so misunderstood," added Congresswoman-elect Jo Ann Emerson of Missouri.
House Democrats on Monday re-elected Richard Gephardt of Missouri as their minority leader and David Bonior of Michigan as his deputy.
